content.text: SitemapOpen in appSign upSign inMedium LogoGet appWriteSearchSign upSign inMember-only storyIs the Universe Blind?Chamim GulFollow4 min read·Mar 31, 2026ListenShareQuantum physics, consciousness, and the unsettling idea that reality may be reflecting usWhat kind of universe do we actually inhabit?Is it deterministic, structured, lawful, predictable?Or is it fundamentally probabilistic, shaped by uncertainty, randomness, and incomplete knowledge?This tension sits at the core of quantum physics, and at the center of one of the most profound intellectual clashes in history.The Disagreement That Never EndedIn the early 20th century, two giants, Niels Bohr and Albert Einstein, offered competing visions of reality.Bohr accepted the strange conclusions of quantum mechanics: that at the smallest scales, outcomes are not determined until measured. Reality, in this view, is inherently probabilistic.Einstein rejected this. Not because he misunderstood the mathematics, but because he refused to believe that nature itself was fundamentally random.His famous statement, “God does not play dice”, was not about religion. It was about order.
